description: We are a team passionate about space, astronomy, technology, and creative problem-solving. We enjoy using AI, software development, data analysis, and visualization to turn complex NASA data into engaging experiences. For the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, we aim to create an interactive way to explore the sky, discover interesting objects, and investigate changes over time.
summary:
SkyTrace, built by Team Alt+F4 for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, is a web-based explorer that turns real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations into an interactive view of the sky across time.

The challenge is that spotting potential changes or unusual objects in vast survey archives is difficult: observations arrive as complex FITS files at different dates and wavelengths, with gaps, quality flags, and alignment uncertainties. SkyTrace addresses this by retrieving authentic DR1/QR3 data from NASA/IPAC IRSA, processing calibrated images and quality masks, and registering observations to a common celestial coordinate grid.

Users can select a sky region, detector, and wavelength range; browse dated epochs; blink or compare images side by side; focus with a freehand lasso; inspect quality overlays; and view Gaia DR3 and AllWISE reference sources. The platform includes 22 genuine exposures across five featured sky fields, with provenance and evidence panels explaining the reliability of each comparison. Real-image subtraction is deliberately disabled until further scientific validation.

SkyTrace matters because an apparent difference is not automatically an astronomical discovery. By making authentic space data accessible while exposing uncertainty, it helps students, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts explore the infrared sky responsibly and lays a foundation for future investigations of celestial change.
details:
SkyTrace | Team Alt+F4

SkyTrace is an interactive astronomical exploration platform developed by Team Alt+F4 for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project addresses the challenge of making complex infrared astronomy data more accessible, understandable, and useful for exploring how the sky changes over time.

SkyTrace transforms authentic observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission into an intuitive, web-based experience. Users can select celestial coordinates, choose among six SPHEREx detectors, filter observations by date and wavelength, and explore images captured at different epochs. The platform includes timeline playback, blinking between observations, side-by-side comparisons, freehand lasso selection to focus on specific sky regions, data-quality mask overlays, and tools for examining apparent positional changes. Gaia DR3 and AllWISE catalogue overlays provide additional astronomical context by displaying reference source positions.

Behind the interface, SkyTrace uses a scientific processing pipeline that retrieves real SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 data from NASA/IPAC IRSA. It processes FITS image data, interprets quality flags and uncertainty information, evaluates spectral metadata, and registers observations onto a common celestial coordinate grid using World Coordinate System (WCS) transformations. The platform also provides comparison-quality assessments, observation metadata, original data references, and provenance information. Five featured sky regions containing 22 genuine SPHEREx exposures are included for reliable demonstrations.

Technology Stack: We developed SkyTrace using Next.js, React, and TypeScript for the frontend, and Python with FastAPI for the backend. Scientific processing uses Astropy, Astroquery, NumPy, SciPy, Reproject, and Pillow. GitHub, Docker, automated testing, and browser-testing tools support development and validation. The application operates on conventional computing infrastructure without requiring specialized astronomical hardware.

Our innovation lies in combining scientific transparency with interactive visualization. Rather than presenting astronomical images without context, SkyTrace helps users understand whether apparent differences could result from wavelength variation, missing data, image alignment, or other observational factors. Scientifically unvalidated real-image subtraction is intentionally restricted to avoid misleading conclusions.

Throughout development, our team prioritized authentic NASA data, scientific accuracy, accessibility, responsive design, processing efficiency, reproducibility, and resilience to temporary archive-service failures.

Our intended impact is to make real space-science datasets easier to explore for students, educators, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts. By bridging the gap between complex scientific archives and intuitive visual tools, SkyTrace encourages curiosity, supports evidence-based investigation, and creates a foundation for future research into our dynamic universe.
